security_spec.violation_condition: When CSRRS/CSRRC (or CSRRSI/CSRRCI) executes on pmpaddr CSR while the corresponding PMP entry is in TOR or NAPOT mode and not locked. The riscv_csrrw_do64() function at csr.c:5669 uses the 'reads as' value from pmpaddr_csr_read() as the basis for RMW computation, then writes it back via pmpaddr_csr_write() which stores it directly into addr_reg without restoring the raw underlying bits. For bits NOT in the rs1 write mask, the read-as value overwrites the true underlying register state.
security_spec.summary: CSRRS/CSRRC RMW path uses pmpaddr_csr_read() 'reads-as' value as write-back base, silently corrupting raw addr_reg bits (e.g. TOR G-1) not targeted by rs1 mask

findings.finding: pmpaddr_csr_read correctly implements 'reads as' behavior per spec: for TOR/OFF (G>=1), bits [G-1:0] forced to 0 at line 638; for NAPOT (G>=2), bits [G-2:0] forced to all-ones at line 644. The transformation is applied only to the returned value; underlying addr_reg is not modified, preserving raw bits across mode changes per norm:pmp_addr_retention_on_mode_change.

spec_citations.excerpt: #norm:pmp_napot_addr_read_mask# When G >= 2 and pmpcfg_i.A[1] is set, i.e. the mode is NAPOT, then bits pmpaddr_i[G-2:0] read as all ones. #norm:pmp_tor_off_addr_read_mask# When G >= 1 and pmpcfg_i.A[1] is clear, i.e. the mode is OFF or TOR, then bits pmpaddr_i[G-1:0] read as all zeros.

#norm:pmp_addr_retention_on_mode_change# Although changing pmpcfg_i.A[1] affects the value read from pmpaddr_i, it does not affect the underlying value stored in that register—in particular, pmpaddr_i[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg_i.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF then back to NAPOT.

findings.finding: Stores val directly into addr_reg at line 603 without stripping low don't-care bits. This is spec-compliant: the RISC-V spec does not require writes to mask these bits, and plain CSR writes (CSRW/CSRWI) should store the raw value. The early-return comparison at line 582 correctly compares against the raw addr_reg to avoid unnecessary TLB flushes.

RMW for CSRRS/CSRRC: reads old_value via .read() at line 5661 (returns transformed 'reads as' value for pmpaddr), computes (old_value & ~write_mask) | (new_value & write_mask) at line 5669, writes back via .write() at line 5671. This is ISA-mandated behavior: the spec NOTE at zicsr.adoc:55-61 explicitly documents that CSRRS/CSRRC will overwrite underlying bits when 'reads as' bits differ from raw bits, using pmpaddr[G-1] as the canonical example. The normative exception rs1=x0 (no write) is handled at line 5668: write_mask==0 skips the write.

spec_citations.excerpt: Since CSRRS and CSRRC perform a read-modify-write operation, any bits that read as a different value to their underlying value may be modified by these instructions even if the corresponding bit is not set in rs1. For example, pmpaddr_n[G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 but read as 0. Executing CSRRC or CSRRS to modify a different bit will cause 0 to be read from pmpaddr_n[G-1] and then written back, updating the underlying value to 0.

norm:csrrs_csrrc_rs1_x0 — For both CSRRS and CSRRC, if rs1=x0, then the instruction will not write to the CSR at all, and so shall not cause any of the side effects that might otherwise occur on a CSR write.

findings.finding: Thin wrapper around pmpaddr_csr_read(), correctly maps csrno to pmpaddr index via csrno - CSR_PMPADDR0 and returns the transformed 'reads as' value. No issues.
Thin wrapper around pmpaddr_csr_write(), correctly maps csrno to pmpaddr index. The write path stores value directly without bit stripping, which is correct for a plain CSR write. No issues.

All 64 pmpaddr CSR entries registered with predicate=pmp, read=read_pmpaddr, write=write_pmpaddr, op=NULL. The NULL op field means CSRRS/CSRRC fall through to separate read-then-write in riscv_csrrw_do64(), which is correct: the spec explicitly says RMW operates on the read-as value, not the raw bits. An .op callback working on raw bits would deviate from ISA-mandated behavior.
findings.snippet:
[CSR_PMPADDR0]   = { "pmpaddr0",  pmp, read_pmpaddr, write_pmpaddr },
[CSR_PMPADDR1]   = { "pmpaddr1",  pmp, read_pmpaddr, write_pmpaddr },
